nodes.en: 【1】In an RGB representation, each pixel in an image is stored as a tuple of (r, g, b) values. The format of an image’s row is (r g b) (r g b) … (r g b), as illustrated in the following conceptual picture. Each tuple specifies a mixture of red (R), green (G) and blue (B). That is, for each pixel, the r, g, and b values represent the intensity (0 being dark and 1 being full intensity) of the red, green, and blue light sources when the pixel is rendered【/1】.
nodes.zh: 【1】在 RGB 表示中，图像中的每个像素存储为 (r, g, b) 值的一个元组。图像一行的格式是 (r g b) (r g b) … (r g b)，如下面的示意图所示。每个元组指定红色（R）、绿色（G）和蓝色（B）的一种混合。也就是说，对每个像素而言，r、g、b 的值分别表示渲染该像素时红、绿、蓝三种光源的强度（0 表示暗，1 表示全强度）【/1】。

nodes.en: 【1】The actual allowable mixtures of these three colors vary across industry-specified color spaces. Here, the valid combinations of the three colors in the AdbobeRGB™ color space are shown as the interior of the triangle. The vertical coordinate (y value) and horizontal coordinate (x value) of each mixture show the fraction of the pixel intensity that should be G and R. The remaining fraction (1-y–x) of the pixel intensity should be assigned to B. To render an image, the r, g, b values of each pixel are used to calculate both the total intensity (luminance) of the pixel as well as the mixture coefficients (x, y, 1-y-x)【/1】.
nodes.zh: 【1】这三种颜色的实际允许混合方式因行业规定的色彩空间而异。这里，AdbobeRGB™ 色彩空间中三种颜色的有效组合显示为三角形的内部区域。每种混合的纵坐标（y 值）和横坐标（x 值）表示像素强度中应分配给 G 和 R 的比例，像素强度的剩余比例 (1-y–x) 应分配给 B。要渲染一幅图像，需要使用每个像素的 r、g、b 值来计算该像素的总强度（亮度）以及混合系数 (x, y, 1-y-x)【/1】。

nodes.en: If we consider the input to be an image organized as an array 【1】I【/1】 of RGB values and the output to be a corresponding array 【2】O【/2】 of luminance values, we get the simple computation structure shown in 【3】Fig. 2.2【/3】. For example, 【4】O【/4】[0] is generated by calculating the weighted sum of the RGB values in 【5】I【/5】[0] according to the formula above; 【6】O【/6】[1] is generated by calculating the weighted sum of the RGB values in 【7】I【/7】[1]; 【8】O【/8】[2] is generated by calculating the weighted sum of the RGB values in 【9】I【/9】[2]; and so on. None of these per-pixel computations depend on each other. All of them can be performed independently. Clearly, color-to-grayscale conversion exhibits a rich amount of data parallelism. Of course, data parallelism in complete applications can be more complex, and much of this book is devoted to teaching the parallel thinking necessary to find and exploit data parallelism.
nodes.zh: 如果我们将输入视为按 RGB 值数组【1】I【/1】组织的一幅图像，将输出视为相应的亮度值数组【2】O【/2】，就得到【3】图 2.2【/3】所示的简单计算结构。例如，【4】O【/4】[0] 是通过按上面的公式计算【5】I【/5】[0] 中 RGB 值的加权和得到的；【6】O【/6】[1] 是通过计算【7】I【/7】[1] 中 RGB 值的加权和得到的；【8】O【/8】[2] 是通过计算【9】I【/9】[2] 中 RGB 值的加权和得到的；依此类推。这些逐像素的计算互不依赖，全部可以独立执行。显然，彩色到灰度转换展现出丰富的数据并行性。当然，完整应用中的数据并行可能更为复杂，而本书有相当多的篇幅正是用于讲解发现和利用数据并行所必需的并行思维。

nodes.en: Task Parallelism vs. Data Parallelism
nodes.zh: 任务并行与数据并行

nodes.en: 【1】Data parallelism is not the only type of parallelism used in parallel programming. Task parallelism has also been used extensively in parallel programming. Task parallelism is typically exposed through task decomposition of applications. For example, a simple application may need to do a vector addition and a matrix-vector multiplication. Each of these would be a task. Task parallelism exists if the two tasks can be done independently. I/O and data transfers are also common sources of tasks【/1】.
nodes.zh: 【1】数据并行并不是并行编程中使用的唯一一种并行方式，任务并行也在并行编程中被广泛使用。任务并行通常通过应用的任务分解来体现。例如，一个简单的应用可能需要做一次向量加法和一次矩阵-向量乘法，其中的每一个都是一个任务。如果这两个任务可以独立完成，就存在任务并行。I/O 和数据传输也是常见的任务来源【/1】。

nodes.en: 【1】In large applications, there are usually a larger number of independent tasks and therefore larger amount of task parallelism. For example, in a molecular dynamics simulator, the list of natural tasks includes vibrational forces, rotational forces, neighbor identification for non-bonding forces, non-bonding forces, velocity and position, and other physical properties based on velocity and position【/1】.
nodes.zh: 【1】在大型应用中，通常会有更多的独立任务，因此也就有更大程度的任务并行。例如，在分子动力学模拟器中，自然任务清单包括振动作用力、转动作用力、非键合力的邻居识别、非键合力、速度与位置，以及基于速度与位置的其他物理属性【/1】。

nodes.en: 【1】In general, data parallelism is the main source of scalability for parallel programs. With large datasets, one can often find abundant data parallelism to be able to utilize massively parallel processors and allow application performance to grow with each generation of hardware that has more execution resources. Nevertheless, task parallelism can also play an important role in achieving performance goals. We will be covering task parallelism later when we introduce streams【/1】.
nodes.zh: 【1】一般来说，数据并行是并行程序可扩展性的主要来源。面对大规模数据集，人们通常能发现丰富的数据并行，从而充分利用大规模并行处理器，让应用性能随着每一代拥有更多执行资源的硬件而增长。尽管如此，任务并行在实现性能目标方面也能发挥重要作用。我们将在后文引入流（streams）时再讨论任务并行【/1】。

nodes.en: 【1】【2】Figure 2.2【/2】【/1】 Data parallelism in image-to-grayscale conversion. Pixels can be calculated independently of each other.
nodes.zh: 【1】【2】图 2.2【/2】【/1】 图像到灰度转换中的数据并行。各像素可以彼此独立地计算。

nodes.en: 2.2 CUDA C program structure
nodes.zh: 2.2 CUDA C 程序结构

nodes.en: We are now ready to learn how to write a CUDA C program to exploit data parallelism for faster execution. CUDA C【1】【2】1【/2】【/1】 extends the popular ANSI C programming language with minimal new syntax and library functions to let programmers target heterogeneous computing systems containing both CPU cores and massively parallel GPUs. As the name implies, CUDA C is built on NVIDIA’s CUDA platform. CUDA is currently the most mature framework for massively parallel computing. It is broadly used in the high-performance computing industry, with essential tools such as compilers, debuggers, and profilers available on the most common operating systems.
nodes.zh: 我们现在就来学习如何编写一个利用数据并行实现更快执行的 CUDA C 程序。CUDA C【1】【2】1【/2】【/1】以最少的语法和库函数扩展了广受欢迎的 ANSI C 编程语言，让程序员能够面向同时包含 CPU 核心和大规模并行 GPU 的异构计算系统进行编程。顾名思义，CUDA C 建立在 NVIDIA 的 CUDA 平台之上。CUDA 目前是进行大规模并行计算最成熟的框架，在高性能计算行业中得到广泛应用，编译器、调试器和性能分析器等关键工具在主流操作系统上均可使用。

nodes.en: The structure of a CUDA C program reflects the coexistence of a 【1】host【/1】 (CPU) and one or more 【2】devices【/2】 (GPUs) in the computer. Each CUDA C source file can have a mixture of host code and device code. By default, any traditional C program is a CUDA program that contains only host code. One can add device code into any source file. The device code is clearly marked with special CUDA C keywords. The device code includes functions, or 【3】kernels【/3】, whose code is executed in a data-parallel manner.
nodes.zh: CUDA C 程序的结构反映了计算机中【1】主机【/1】（CPU）与一个或多个【2】设备【/2】（GPU）共存这一事实。每个 CUDA C 源文件都可以同时包含主机代码和设备代码。默认情况下，任何传统 C 程序都是一个只包含主机代码的 CUDA 程序。我们可以向任何源文件中添加设备代码，设备代码用特殊的 CUDA C 关键字明确标记。设备代码包含一些函数，即【3】核函数【/3】，这些函数的代码以数据并行方式执行。

nodes.en: The execution of a CUDA program is illustrated in 【1】Fig. 2.3【/1】. The execution starts with host code (CPU serial code). When a kernel function is called, a large number of threads are 【2】launched【/2】 on a device to execute the kernel. All the threads that are launched by a kernel call are collectively called a 【3】grid【/3】. These threads are the primary vehicle of parallel execution in a CUDA platform. 【4】Fig. 2.3【/4】 shows the execution of two grids of threads. We will discuss how these grids are organized soon. When all threads of a grid have completed their execution, the grid terminates, and the execution continues on the host until another grid is launched. Note that 【5】Fig. 2.3【/5】 shows a simplified model in which the CPU execution and the GPU execution do not overlap. Many heterogeneous computing applications manage overlapped CPU and GPU execution to take advantage of both CPUs and GPUs.
nodes.zh: CUDA 程序的执行过程如【1】图 2.3【/1】所示。执行从主机代码（CPU 串行代码）开始。当调用核函数时，会在设备上【2】启动【/2】大量线程来执行该核函数。一次核函数调用所启动的所有线程合称为一个【3】网格【/3】。这些线程是 CUDA 平台上并行执行的主要载体。【4】图 2.3【/4】显示了两个线程网格的执行过程。我们很快会讨论这些网格是如何组织的。当一个网格的所有线程都执行完毕时，该网格终止，执行回到主机上继续，直到启动另一个网格。请注意，【5】图 2.3【/5】显示的是一个简化模型，其中 CPU 执行与 GPU 执行并不重叠。许多异构计算应用会设法让 CPU 与 GPU 的执行相互重叠，以同时发挥 CPU 和 GPU 的优势。

nodes.en: 【1】Figure 2.3【/1】 Execution of a CUDA program.
nodes.zh: 【1】图 2.3【/1】 CUDA 程序的执行。

nodes.en: Launching a grid typically generates many threads to exploit data parallelism. In the color-to-grayscale conversion example, each thread could be used to compute one pixel of the output array O. In this case, the number of threads that ought to be generated by the grid launch is equal to the number of pixels in the image. For large images, a large number of threads will be generated. CUDA programmers can assume that these threads take very few clock cycles to generate and schedule, owing to efficient hardware support. This assumption contrasts with traditional CPU threads, which typically take thousands of clock cycles to generate and schedule. In the next chapter we will show how to implement color-to-grayscale conversion and image blur kernels. In the rest of this chapter we will use vector addition as a running example for simplicity.
nodes.zh: 启动一个网格通常会生成大量线程，以利用数据并行。在彩色到灰度转换的例子中，每个线程可用来计算输出数组 O 的一个像素。此时，网格启动应生成的线程数等于图像中的像素数。对于大图像，将生成大量的线程。得益于高效的硬件支持，CUDA 程序员可以假设这些线程的生成与调度只需要很少的时钟周期。这一假设与传统 CPU 线程形成鲜明对比——传统的 CPU 线程通常需要数千个时钟周期来生成和调度。在下一章中，我们将展示如何实现彩色到灰度转换和图像模糊的核函数。为了简单起见，本章其余部分将使用向量加法作为贯穿示例。

nodes.en: Threads
nodes.zh: 线程

nodes.en: 【1】A thread is a simplified view of how a processor executes a sequential program in modern computers. A thread consists of the code of the program, the point in the code that is being executed, and the values of its variables and data structures. The execution of a thread is sequential as far as a user is concerned. One can use a source-level debugger to monitor the progress of a thread by executing one statement at a time, looking at the statement that will be executed next and checking the values of the variables and data structures as the execution progresses【/1】.
nodes.zh: 【1】线程是现代计算机中处理器如何执行串行程序的一种简化视图。一个线程由程序的代码、代码中正在执行的执行点，以及其变量和数据结构的取值构成。就用户而言，线程的执行是串行的。我们可以使用源代码级调试器来监视线程的执行进度：一次执行一条语句，查看下一条将要执行的语句，并在执行过程中检查变量和数据结构的取值【/1】。

nodes.en: 【1】Threads have been used in programming for many years. If a programmer wants to start parallel execution in an application, he/she creates and manages multiple threads using thread libraries or special languages. In CUDA, the execution of each thread is sequential as well. A CUDA program initiates parallel execution by calling kernel functions, which causes the underlying runtime mechanisms to launch a grid of threads that process different parts of the data in parallel【/1】.
nodes.zh: 【1】线程在编程中已经使用了很多年。如果程序员想在应用中启动并行执行，他/她会使用线程库或专用语言来创建并管理多个线程。在 CUDA 中，每个线程的执行同样也是串行的。CUDA 程序通过调用核函数来启动并行执行，这会促使底层的运行时机制启动一个线程网格，并行处理数据的不同部分【/1】。

nodes.en: 2.3 A vector addition kernel
nodes.zh: 2.3 向量加法核函数

nodes.en: We use vector addition to demonstrate the CUDA C program structure. Vector addition is arguably the simplest possible data parallel computation—the parallel equivalent of “Hello World” from sequential programming. Before we show the kernel code for vector addition, it is helpful to first review how a conventional vector addition (host code) function works. 【1】Fig. 2.4【/1】 shows a simple traditional C program that consists of a main function and a vector addition function. In all our examples, whenever there is a need to distinguish between host and device data, we will suffix the names of variables that are used by the host with “【2】_h【/2】” and those of variables that are used by a device with “【3】_d【/3】” to remind ourselves of the intended usage of these variables. Since we have only host code in 【4】Fig. 2.4【/4】, we see only variables suffixed with “【5】_h【/5】”.
nodes.zh: 我们使用向量加法来演示 CUDA C 程序的结构。向量加法可以说是最简单的一种数据并行计算——相当于串行编程中的“Hello World”。在展示向量加法的核函数代码之前，先回顾一下传统的向量加法（主机代码）函数是如何工作的，会很有帮助。【1】图 2.4【/1】显示了一个由 main 函数和一个向量加法函数组成的简单传统 C 程序。在本书的所有示例中，只要需要区分主机数据和设备数据，我们就会给主机使用的变量名加上“【2】_h【/2】”后缀，给设备使用的变量名加上“【3】_d【/3】”后缀，以提醒自己这些变量的用途。由于【4】图 2.4【/4】中只有主机代码，所以我们只看到以“【5】_h【/5】”为后缀的变量。

nodes.en: Pointers in the C Language
nodes.zh: C 语言中的指针

nodes.en: 【1】The function arguments A, B, and C in【/1】 【2】Fig. 2.4【/2】 【3】are pointers. In the C language, a pointer can be used to access variables and data structures. While a floating-point variable V can be declared with:【/3】
nodes.zh: 【1】【2】图 2.4【/2】中的函数实参 A、B 和 C【/1】【3】都是指针。在 C 语言中，指针可以用来访问变量和数据结构。例如，浮点变量 V 可以这样声明：【/3】

nodes.en: 【1】float V;【/1】
nodes.zh: 可以用【1】float V;【/1】来声明。

nodes.en: 【1】a pointer variable P can be declared with:【/1】
nodes.zh: 【1】指针变量 P 可以这样声明：【/1】

nodes.en: 【1】float *P;【/1】
nodes.zh: 可以用【1】float *P;【/1】来声明。

nodes.en: 【1】By assigning the address of V to P with the statement P=&V, we make P “point to” V. *P becomes a synonym for V. For example, U=*P assigns the value of V to U. For another example, *P=3 changes the value of V to 3【/1】.
nodes.zh: 【1】通过语句 P=&V 把 V 的地址赋给 P，我们让 P“指向”V。此时 *P 成为 V 的同义词。例如，U=*P 会把 V 的值赋给 U；再如，*P=3 会把 V 的值改为 3【/1】。
